articles.title: This is Lumeah / Pepper & Well
articles.summary: Lumeah is a careful renovation of one of the most intact houses designed by modernist architect Paul Couch. Located in Macedon on Wurundjeri Woi Wurrung Country, the house—formerly known as the Harley House—was conceived as a highly resolved composition of exposed concrete, bluestone, timber, stainless steel and compressed-straw Stramit Board, without a painted surface.

articles.title: WA SSL House / AZAZ Architects
articles.summary: Wa ssl, meaning connection, is a private retreat designed by Azaz Architects and constructed by LayCon, located dramatically on the edge of a cliff overlooking the Alwasseel valley in Al Jubaylah. The project was conceived by a family seeking a place of gathering and retreat—a counterpoint to the noise, density, and accelerated rhythm of life in the city. articles.title: When Security Becomes Part of the Architecture
articles.summary: What transforms a space of living into a home ? Beyond ownership or shelter, a home is tied to a quieter sense of certainty: the feeling that one can retreat, rest, and momentarily step away from the world's unpredictability. Homes are where routines accumulate, memories settle into spaces and objects, and where personal identity takes physical form through occupation and everyday rituals. Yet this sense of belonging depends on another condition that often goes unnoticed until disrupted: security . To feel "at home" implies a condition of comfort and stability. articles.title: House in Los Cóndores / Malachowski Arquitectos
articles.summary: This single-family home in Los Cóndores, on the outskirts of Lima, is born from a clear decision: to let the slope of the site organize the project. The result is a sequence of platforms, roofs, and open spaces that follow the natural topography, turning the journey—climbing, crossing, pausing—into the core of the domestic experience.

articles.title: Casa Itu / Nitsche Arquitetos
articles.summary: The choice of the site was the starting point for the Casa Itu project. After several months of visiting and analyzing different sites, considering topography, sun exposure, and the surrounding context, we selected a corner lot with a slope oriented toward a pleasant landscape and north, the most favorable orientation in the region.

articles.title: Florinda House / Alvariño & Felipe Arquitectos
articles.summary: Casa Florinda began with a question: what to do with the old earthen house that stood in ruins on the land we had acquired to build our home? Although our first plans involved tearing it down, something about the way it belonged to the site prevented us from doing so. The decision to preserve it ultimately intertwined two dimensions of our lives: living and making architecture. Thus, the old structure would become our home and the place where we would test our own convictions about architecture.

articles.summary: The building was designed as a sober and simple volume that is reminiscent of an old atelier or a small-scale classic industrial building. articles.title: Izzy Swan Revolutionizes Workbench Hold-Down
articles.summary: Not too long ago, in order to have vacuum hold-down at your workbench, you needed an air compressor and earplugs. Those days are over. This is the VacQube , a diminutive, quiet 12V vacuum pump created by inventor Izzy Swan. The idea is that you drill a hole in your workbench and plug the VacQube's 1/4" airline into the bottom of it. When you drop its companion VacQseal—essentially a gasket—on top of the workbench and encircling the hole, now you've got instant holddown.
